reason: The cited evidence (E1) supports that aging at 750°C produces γ′ precipitates via Al/Ti partitioning in a specific Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni–Ti alloy, but it does not address environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, or cryogenic toughness, leaving three of the four key premises unsupported.
premises: Aging at 750°C induces diffusion-driven partitioning of Al and Ti in Al–Co–Cr–Fe–Ni HEAs
This partitioning nucleates and stabilizes coherent γ′-like precipitates
The precipitates mediate the interplay between solid-solution and precipitate strengthening
This phase separation governs phase stability and enables retention of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness
